# Complete Demo B's native-host effect composition

## Context

This continues #15614's native-host phase. #20515 separated source callbacks and reservation/bind/release routing. Their pane and platform effects still live among gesture and projection methods in `DemoBWorkspace.mjs`.

## The Problem

At `dev b0e5fceb91`, twelve native/pane-effect methods occupy 390 raw lines including their documentation. Reading a source callback in the 385-line `DemoBNativeWindowHost` still requires returning to the large composition host to follow acquisition, adoption, close, rollback and return. These effects have the same consumer-specific responsibility as the adapters already extracted.

## The Architectural Reality

Move exactly:
- `exactTearOutVessel`, `resolveVesselKey`, `resolveTearOutVessel`, `vesselWindowName`;
- `onTearOutDocumentChange`, `applyTearOutOperation`, `recordDockPaneOwner`, `reparentDockPane`;
- `popOutPane`, `openTearOutVessel`, `closeTearOutVessel`, `reattachPane`.

The Group continues owning admission/connection/owner/retirement records. Cache, fields, document participants, source registration lifetime, listeners and destruction remain workspace-owned. Methods moved into the existing prototype mixin still execute on that workspace.

`NativeVesselTransaction` remains the shared Dock mechanism. The #19296 lineage deliberately keeps app policy outside the generic Transaction owner; this slice changes neither shared mechanism nor policy. Existing host calls and distinct failure rules must survive:

1. Exact retirement routes include the Group's pending-retirement stamp. An invalid exact route must not become a same-name fallback close.
2. Placement is captured before detach. Terminal-first pane preservation is chosen before publication; adoption resolves current collaborators/connection after the awaited document change.
3. Click-popout opening failure compensates from the committed participant's `before` placement.
4. Reattach commits home ownership and deletes bookkeeping before awaiting native close; close failure still reports `reattached: true`.
5. Tear-out cancellation restores the inner proxy before the outer embodiment through the existing shared close helper.

Design authority: n/a — preserves existing behavior to fulfill the parent's maintenance/decomposition intent.

Prescription checked: `DemoBNativeWindowHost.mjs` — its registered source callbacks already call these effects. Euclid's independent source read supports extending that adapter rather than creating another helper or state owner.

## The Fix

Extend the existing `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBNativeWindowHost.mjs`; delete the old implementations from `DemoBWorkspace.mjs`.

Retain the four semantic-ID-bearing methods as thin host facades: `onTearOutDocumentChange`, `applyTearOutOperation`, `popOutPane`, `reattachPane`. Give their internal implementations distinct names and pass the existing main/popup IDs explicitly. Other methods remain host-callable through the mixin. Preserve defaults, promises, return shapes and current host dispatch after waits; no import back to DemoBWorkspace.

Keep gesture execution, the cross-window commit core, projection, perspective handling and all lifetime ownership outside this move. Re-measure both files and the combined source after facades/docs; the preliminary 385+390 count is not the final result.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Preserved behavior | Failure / fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact vessel resolution/close | Group native lifecycle and NativeVesselTransaction | Same source-scoped keys and exact route stamp | Same refusal/retry; no weaker name fallback | Method JSDoc | Existing route/retirement units |
| Detach publication/adoption | Current host, WorkspaceSet and TearOut | Placement before detach; preservation before publication; current post-await collaborators | Same rejected-operation capture cleanup | Method JSDoc | Existing lifecycle/race controls and native tear-out |
| Click pop-out | Current two-document transfer and native open | Same receipt, reservation and same-pane move | Compensate from committed before placement on open failure | Method JSDoc | Existing rollback units and pop-out native witness |
| Reattach | Current transfer/close order | Commit and bookkeeping removal precede native close | Semantic return remains true if close fails | Method JSDoc | Existing close-failure/unit and native return coverage |
| Host lifetime | Current constructor and destroy | Same fields, source lifetime, cache and collaborators | Existing teardown | Class JSDoc | Existing workspace/lifecycle suite |

Decision Record impact: aligned-with `neomjs/neo#adr:docking-design`; no new policy or protocol.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The twelve effects live beside their existing native source adapters, with no new class, registry or lifecycle owner; host public methods/facades remain.
- [ ] AC-2: Method behavior is equivalent except explicit semantic-ID parameters and distinct internal names. All five preservation boundaries above remain intact; do not consolidate failure policies.
- [ ] AC-3: Existing DemoBWorkspace/TourRunner and full Engine unit suites pass without weakened expectations. Add two bounded preservation controls: publication deferred while the adoption collaborator/connection changes, and a native close exception during explicit reattach after semantic ownership has returned. Prove both controls against the unchanged source before extraction.
- [ ] AC-4: Five existing headed journeys pass: DemoBPopOutCloseNL, the two-run DemoBPerspectivesNL tour, DemoBDockTearOutNL's middle-tab commit and plain cancellation, and DemoBCrossWindowDragNL's Escape-after-remote-preview journey. They cover pane return, explicit reattach, commit/catalog/sibling order and nested unwind. Record exact scope/environment separately from CI; retain failed runs and classify before retrying. Parent-final row-4/5 acceptance remains separate and open.
- [ ] AC-5: Full JSDoc/`@summary`, correct host-qualified links, measured host/module/combined counts and a lowered host size baseline. Update the parent inventory without claiming raw-target or final matrix completion.

## Out of Scope

New acquisition/close/rollback policy; generic transaction or native lifecycle changes; park/re-show behavior; Workspace superclass migration; gesture driver, perspectives or tour extraction; cross-window commit-core moves; multi-OS certification; parent closure.

## Avoided Traps

Do not turn three different failure policies into one generic rollback function. Do not capture stale collaborators or duplicate Group records on the host. Do not overwrite a public facade with a same-named mixin implementation. Extend the existing adapter rather than minting a sibling abstraction. Raw counts from independent branches are not cumulative integration evidence.
